extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and reviewers (career development K award applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required content for sections of an NIH career-development (K) / investigator-initiated grant application, including methodology, human subjects protection, institutional environment, training, inclusion policies, data sharing, and resource/authentication statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and power considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: For all Aims, the number of events in each exposure category should be sufficiently large to accommodate inferences with adequate power (example retention/treatment/viral suppression proportions provided from NA-ACCORD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses observed cohort proportions (e.g., 71% retained, 82% prescribed treatment, 78% had HIV RNA ≤200 copies/mL) to assess power. Power for piecewise GLMM analyses would be similar to that for Aim 1. Ensure event counts within exposure categories are sufficient for planned inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical model specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Piecewise generalized linear mixed model specified as: Logit(πij) = (β0+b0i) + (β00+b00i)*post-ACA + (β1+b1i)*tij*pre-ACA + (β2+b2i)*tij*post-ACA + βx*X, with random effects b0i, b00i for intercepts and b1i, b2i for slopes (each ~ N(0,σ2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail fixed and random effects, time terms pre/post policy, and covariates (βx*X). Provide appropriate random-effects structure and justify model choice for longitudinal/quasi-experimental analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity analyses for unmeasured confounding and missing data
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensitivity analyses will be conducted for inclusion of unmeasured confounding (using methods of Cornfield); data missingness will be explored (e.g., CD4+ at entry); if data are missing within sites, multiple imputation techniques will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state methods for assessing unmeasured confounding, describe missing-data diagnostics, and prespecify imputation approaches as appropriate. Cite methods (e.g., Cornfield) and references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of advanced modeling and methods for transportability
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional techniques such as agent-based modeling may be employed to explore plausible effects under different policy decisions and behaviors; spatial statistical techniques and inverse probability of selection weighting may be used to address spatial/temporal variability and transportability/generalizability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify use of cutting-edge or alternative methods for policy/program questions, identify input parameters (e.g., from observational research), and acknowledge limitations/ongoing research about applying selection-weighting to program/policy questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and milestones (deliverables and PI responsibilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed timeline across Years 1–5 listing tasks (data cleaning, analyses), deliverables (conference presentations, manuscript submissions), internal peer-review, and an R01 grant writing/submission plan (initial submission dates and plans for resubmission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a year-by-year schedule, specify PI/mentor/committee roles, list concrete deliverables per Aim (abstracts, manuscripts, visualizations), and include realistic assumptions (e.g., data lag).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training in the responsible conduct of research is required for all faculty engaged in human subjects research at VUSM and JHSPH; applicant will enroll in VUSM BRET RCR session and PUBH 5518 'Research Ethics in Health Policy'. Topics include ethics, data management, research fraud, misconduct, conflict of interest, vulnerable populations, confidentiality, IRB processes, informed consent, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify planned RCR coursework (face-to-face sessions, semester-long courses), track attendance/completion via institutional offices, describe how RCR topics will be integrated into the candidate's presentations and mentorship activities, and list institutional resources used for RCR training.

rubrics_metrics.name: CITI Human Research certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Completion and certification of the online 'Human Research' CITI module (required by VUSM and JHSPH IRBs) with sections including the Belmont Report, history and ethical principles, IRB regulations and process, informed consent, research with protected/vulnerable subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include certification evidence in appendix and maintain current CITI certification as required by institutional IRBs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor, co-mentor, and mentoring committee qualifications and involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentors and collaborators are experienced human subjects researchers with knowledge of data collection, management, security, sharing, authorship, collaborations, and peer review; mentors also serve on data safety monitoring boards and IRBs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe mentors' qualifications, their roles in oversight and training, and how their expertise will support ethical conduct, data security, and methodological guidance for the candidate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of institutional environment and available resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Document institutional strengths (Vanderbilt's large medical center, NIH funding rank, Departmental funding), specialized centers and resources (VICTR, StarBRITE, REDCap, Studios, CTSD, manuscript/grant writing support, Biostatistics clinics, BCC, ACCRE, Health Policy Department), and relevant clinical cohorts/clinics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate access to core facilities, data/biostatistics support, educational programs, pilot funding, and collaborative groups; explain how these resources will be used to support the proposed work and career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects involvement and population characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of existing cohort data (NA-ACCORD and CCASAnet) on adults ≥18 with at least one CD4, viral load, or clinic visit; estimated sample sizes and age distribution provided; pediatric patients and those without clinic encounter data excluded for certain Aims; vulnerable populations are not specifically targeted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear inclusion/exclusion criteria, population descriptors, and rationale for excluded groups where relevant to aims. Explicitly state that no additional information is required from individual subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of materials and data management responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Existent 'on the shelf' electronic data from participating clinical cohorts transmitted to NA-ACCORD and CCASAnet Data Management Cores using centrally assembled submission documents; only elements required for approved protocols are maintained; cohorts perform data mapping and routine data audits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe data transmission, harmonization, mapping, quality control/audit procedures, and which data elements will be retained. Identify Data Management Core responsibilities and location (University of Washington, Vanderbilt).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data de-identification and HIPAA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: All information maintained and transmitted to analysis cores will be de-identified per HIPAA; geographic data: individuals in 3-digit ZIP areas with populations <20,000 have ZIP entered as '000'; subjects assigned unique study identifiers distinct from parent cohort identifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State de-identification methods, masking/suppression rules for small-area geography, creation/use of study IDs, and assertion that no NA-ACCORD/CCASAnet staff will have access to individually identifiable private information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment, consent, and IRB approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: No additional recruitment or direct subject contact; cohorts and consortia maintain existing IRB approvals; a waiver of informed consent will be requested from the Vanderbilt IRB prior to the start of funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document institutional IRB approvals for parent cohorts and the plan for waivers when using de-identified existing data. Ensure each contributing cohort maintains its IRB approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections against risk and data security measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Perceived risks are minimal because data are de-identified. Security measures include five levels of security monitored (user access, data access, NFS export access, tape security, monitoring for damaging software), domain controller for managing user IDs/access, restricted access to servers/directories, limited local DB access to administrators, and use of SSL for secure transfers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail technical and administrative safeguards: firewalled equipment, domain controllers, user/group access controls for web/data management, limitation of local DB admin rights, required secure protocols (SSL), and disabling insecure protocols (telnet/ftp).

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential risks, benefits, and importance of knowledge to be gained
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be no direct benefit to subjects; minimal risks are reasonable in relation to anticipated benefits to research participants, HIV-infected populations, and public health via improved policy/interventions. Findings could guide interventions, funding, and tracking progress toward national goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a balanced assessment of minimal risk vs potential societal/public health benefits, and describe how results could inform policy and future research priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of women and minorities
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be no exclusions based on sex or race/ethnicity; preliminary enrollment estimates and detailed racial composition are provided in enrollment tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include PHS Inclusion Enrollment Report data, present demographic breakdowns by sex, race, and ethnicity, and justify inclusion/exclusion decisions per NIH policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of children (NIH policy and justification)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH defines children as under 18; NA-ACCORD pre-enrolls only those ≥18, so no children included. CCASAnet has pediatric cohorts but they will not be included; this fulfills NIH exclusionary circumstances for collecting additional data on pre-enrolled adults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State NIH definition, explain rationale for excluding children (study design/insufficient geographic heterogeneity or applicability), and reference relevant NIH policy citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select agent research statement
rubrics_metrics.description: NOT APPLICABLE — proposal does not involve select agent research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit statement when select agent research is not involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource sharing plan
rubrics_metrics.description: All data acquired through NIH funds and conduct of the proposed research will be shared and made publicly available through publication in the peer-reviewed literature. The application does not request direct costs ≥ $500,000 in any single year, does not involve model organisms, and is not a genome-wide association study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear data/resource sharing plan compliant with NIH expectations; note any exceptions or specific resource-sharing mechanisms and whether large-cost or GWAS/resource-intensive conditions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of key biological and/or chemical resources
rubrics_metrics.description: NOT APPLICABLE — proposal does not utilize key biological and/or chemical resources; therefore there are no resources to be authenticated/validated prior to work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, describe authentication/validation procedures; if not applicable, include an explicit statement as done here.
